importance_ranking.reason: Visual style variation across bamboo hut sub-types is extreme — a Bali-style hut, a thatched beach hut, a gazebo, and a tree house are visually unrecognisable as the same product category. Hospitality buyers have a specific aesthetic brief; image is the primary style selector and wrong aesthetic means immediate skip.

Built type (prefab vs on-site), treatment quality, and floor area are non-interchangeable shortlisting gates — untreated bamboo lasts 1–3 years vs chemical-treated at 15–25 years, making treatment a compliance and durability decision, not a preference. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated for resort or commercial deployment.

Indian hospitality buyers compare per-sq-ft rates aggressively but only after confirming style and treatment spec match — a prefab chemical-treated Bali hut and an untreated on-site garden hut are not price-comparable. Listed price is a budget entry point; final price is always negotiated based on custom dimensions and specifications.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per piece (small fixed-size garden huts) or per project (full site-fabricated structures) — per sq ft vs per piece creates real price comparison confusion and must be shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing the unit — per sq ft, per piece, and per project are all active in this market and represent fundamentally different pricing bases. Unit ambiguity directly misleads buyers comparing rates.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in the Indian bamboo hut market — the market is fragmented across regional fabricators and no sibling MCAT carves out a branded sub-segment; buyers search by style and treatment spec, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Seller installation capability, service geography (pan-India vs regional), and track record of resort/hospitality projects are evaluated during vendor selection for a large custom structure, but only after style and spec shortlisting is complete.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Treatment class (untreated vs chemical treated) drives the largest price delta in this category and is non-interchangeable — a resort buyer cannot substitute untreated bamboo for chemical-treated given the 1–3 year vs 15–25 year lifespan difference.

Prefab, knock-down, and on-site build represent fundamentally different delivery and installation models with significant cost and lead-time differences — a buyer requiring prefab cannot substitute on-site build.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Wall construction type (bamboo poles, bamboo matting panels, thatch panels) is a primary visual and structural differentiator that determines both the aesthetic outcome and the structural integrity of the hut — absent from the current spec list despite being a core buyer decision variable.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Design style defines the structural form and aesthetic (Gazebo vs Bali Style vs Cottage vs Hut Shape) — sellers need this to determine which product line applies and whether they can supply the required design.
Floor dimensions drive material quantity, structural feasibility, and per-sq-ft pricing — sellers cannot generate an accurate quote without knowing the required footprint.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Bamboo treatment class (untreated vs chemical treated vs heat treated) determines the structure's lifespan and compliance suitability for commercial hospitality use — sellers need this to confirm product durability tier and price accurately.
